candidateEvidence.excerpt: Claude is folding quick questions and longer Cowork jobs into one conversation

Anthropic announced September 16 that it is merging Claude chat and Cowork into one Claude experience. A person can ask a quick question or hand over a longer, multi-step task without choosing a mode first.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Starting today, Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude.

This is rolling out to Pro and Max plans first, in the Claude app on web, desktop, and mobile over the coming weeks to existing and new users on these plans. There’s nothing to turn on. Team and Free plans will follow soon, and Enterprise admins will hear from us at least 30 days before anything changes for their organizations.

scopeAndFreshness: P002 matches the official blog passage 'Starting today, Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude' dated September 16, with correct attribution to Anthropic and no mode-choice needed, matching 'There's nothing to turn on.'

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Rollout is gradual: Pro and Max first across web, desktop and mobile. Team and Free follow; Enterprise gets at least 30 days’ notice. Same-plan accounts may differ.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: LAiDIES would use the longer-work option when a task has named inputs and a document to check. Anthropic says Manual asks before actions; Auto reduces check-ins. The setting covers the conversation. Those are vendor descriptions, not proof a task will finish well.
“Claude is removing the mode choice, not the need to choose permissions.”

sourceEvidence.excerpt:
Auto: Claude keeps working without stopping to ask about each step, and automated safety checks run before it takes an action.
Manual (default): Claude asks before it takes actions, and you choose whether to allow each one.
The setting applies to the whole conversation.

Tasks that use files or apps on your computer need Claude Desktop open.
More involved tasks keep running in the cloud even if you close your laptop

scopeAndFreshness: P005 accurately paraphrases the help documentation: Manual (default) asks before actions, Auto keeps working without stopping about each step, and 'The setting applies to the whole conversation.' Attribution ('Anthropic says') and the vendor-description caveat are retained; omitting Auto's automated safety checks is a conservative omission, not a distortion.
